transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we get too far into the details, I want to frame this conversation around what I need from each of you. As you know, the company plans to roll out the vendor's AI platform for customer-support chats and call transcripts starting next quarter, and I'm the one who gives final approval before we sign. Our contract-approval routine requires privacy, insurance, and customer-contracts counsel to each report any required changes before I sign off. I've reviewed the vendor's draft agreement, and there are a few things that stand out to me already: the vendor reserves the right to use submitted content to improve its services, deletion is promised within 30 days after termination, there's no specified data-residency location, the liability and insurance language is the vendor's standard, and we have no express audit right. I'd like to hear from each of you on whether any of these — or anything else in the draft — requires changes before I can approve. Let's start with privacy counsel — what are your concerns?

transcript.text: Thanks, Elena. I've reviewed the draft from a privacy perspective, and I have several required changes. First, the vendor's right to use submitted content to improve its services is a problem — our approved data-processing standard prohibits use of customer content for model training or service improvement, so that clause needs to be struck. Second, the 30-day deletion window is insufficient; our standard requires deletion within exactly 7 calendar days after termination. Third, the lack of a specified data-residency location needs to be addressed — our standard requires processing exclusively in the European Union, so we need an explicit data-residency commitment to that effect. These are all mandatory under our approved data-processing standard given that the platform will be processing identifiable customer call transcripts. Let me share the specifics of my findings so everyone has the full picture.
